method: A stabiliser can only move the picture inside the recorded frame, so the crop has to be large enough that the picture never runs out of pixels. The required margin per side is the residual shake in pixels plus the roll in radians multiplied by half the frame diagonal, the distance a corner sits from the centre and therefore the farthest a turn moves any picture point, and the sum is rounded up to a whole pixel. The crop keeps the shot's shape by zooming uniformly: the scale is the short side divided by the short side less twice the margin, so a 3840 x 2160 frame with a 36 px margin scales by 2160 / 2088 = 1.0345, a 3.45 percent zoom, and the kept window is 3712 x 2088 px after both dimensions are floored to an even count. The short side keeps the margin exactly and the long side gives up the same share of its pixels, 64 px rather than 36 px at that default. The field of view kept is the kept width over the source width, and the pixels kept is the kept area over the source area. The budget table inverts the relation: a zoom of z percent gives a short-side margin of shortSide x (1 - 1 / (1 + z / 100)) / 2 and absorbs that margin less the roll margin as shake. Frame width and height must be whole numbers from 64 to 16384 pixels, the shake from 0 to 1000 px and the roll from 0 to 20 degrees, and a margin that would leave less than 64 px on the short side is refused rather than returned. Shake and roll are the residual motion you measure or expect after stabilisation, so the page plans a crop instead of predicting what a particular stabiliser will do; off-centre crops for look-room, rolling-shutter skew, parallax between near and far subjects, motion blur and resampling softening are not modelled. Calculations run entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
